chosen_title: CARsgen makes history as China approves world's first CAR-T therapy for solid tumors
caption:
🔬 For decades, solid tumors have beaten back every CAR-T attempt. That just changed.

China has approved CARsgen Therapeutics' CAR-T cell therapy targeting solid tumors — a global first. The drug homes in on Claudin18.2, a protein overexpressed on cells in gastric, pancreatic, and esophageal cancers, some of the deadliest malignancies in oncology. CAR-T (Chimeric Antigen Receptor T-cell) therapy works by engineering a patient's own immune cells to recognize and destroy cancer, then infusing billions of them back into the body.

Since the first FDA approval in 2017, CAR-T has transformed outcomes in blood cancers like leukemia and lymphoma, with some patients achieving complete remission. But solid tumors — roughly 90% of all human cancers — have consistently neutralized the approach by creating a hostile microenvironment that disarms engineered T-cells. CARsgen's Claudin18.2-targeted therapy appears to have cleared that barrier, at least for select tumor types, becoming the first CAR-T to win regulatory approval for a solid tumor anywhere in the world.

Why it matters: This is proof-of-concept that CAR-T can breach solid tumors, potentially opening a new era of immunotherapy for the cancers that kill the most people. US and European regulators will be watching closely.

Source: Fierce Pharma

slides.label: THE STORY
slides.headline: A Decades-Long Wall Just Fell
slides.body: China has approved CARsgen Therapeutics' CAR-T cell therapy targeting solid tumors — a global first in cancer medicine. The drug targets Claudin18.2, a protein overexpressed on certain solid tumor cells including gastric and pancreatic cancers. CAR-T therapy has revolutionized blood cancer treatment since 2017, but solid tumors had blocked every previous attempt — creating a wall researchers spent decades trying to breach.

slides.label: THE NUMBER
slides.caption: Roughly 90% of all human cancers are solid tumors — the very cancer type that CAR-T therapy has failed to treat for decades, making this China approval a landmark turning point.
slides.headline: of All Cancers Are Solid Tumors

slides.label: HOW IT WORKS
slides.headline: Your Own Cells, Reprogrammed to Kill
slides.body: CAR-T extracts a patient's T-cells, engineers them in a lab with a receptor that locks onto a cancer-specific protein — here, Claudin18.2 — then infuses billions back into the body as living drugs. Solid tumors had long defeated this by creating an immunosuppressive microenvironment that disarms the engineered cells on arrival.

slides.label: WHY IT MATTERS
points: CARsgen's therapy targets Claudin18.2, a protein overexpressed on gastric, pancreatic, and esophageal cancer cells, giving engineered T-cells a precise molecular target so they attack tumors without destroying healthy tissue.

CAR-T drugs transformed blood cancer care after the first FDA approval in 2017, but solid tumors — responsible for the overwhelming majority of global cancer deaths — had resisted every prior CAR-T approach.

China's approval is the first time any CAR-T therapy has cleared a national regulator for a solid tumor anywhere in the world, setting a direct precedent for future regulatory submissions in the US and Europe.

If the Claudin18.2 approach proves broadly applicable, it could eventually extend to other tumor types that express the same protein, targeting some of the most treatment-resistant cancers in all of oncology.
